name: MapHoverCard
intent: The card shown while hovering a map marker — a peek at what is under the cursor.
when: A map marker needs identifying without opening its full record
Several kinds of marker share a map and each should say something different on hover

chooseOver.because: HoverCard is the generic Radix trigger-and-content pair for DOM elements. MapHoverCard is only the card: map markers are plain DOM outside React, so the map widget owns the trigger and placement.
chooseOver.avoidOverride: Wrap a map marker in a Radix HoverCard trigger

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting the full record in the hover card
commonMistakes.fix: Carry only what identifies the thing and what you would decide on; opening it is what the detail panel is for
commonMistakes.avoidOverride: Duplicate the detail panel's content on hover

lineage.confidence: unset — all three marker kinds hovered and read back in the browser

props.name: badges
props.description: Badges or meta under the title.

props.name: media
props.description: A preview strip above the title — a camera still, an image, a chart.

props.name: rows
props.description: Label/value lines. Keep it to a handful; this is a peek, not the record.

props.name: footer
props.description: A closing line — a hint, a count, an action.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All standard HTML attributes are supported.

usage: Use MapHoverCard to structure and organize content within your interface. This component helps create visual hierarchy and consistent spacing throughout your application.
MapHoverCard works well for arranging related content, creating responsive layouts, and maintaining visual consistency. Use it to group related elements and establish clear content boundaries.

bestPractices.description: Avoid heavy shadows on every card, reserve for interactive or important items.
